Logistic Growth
::: {style="font-size: 70%;"} Applied Population Dynamics\ WILD 5700/7700 :::
## Today in APD
The equation for logistic growth in discrete time.
The definition of density-dependent growth.
Basic properties of the model.
Strange behavior of the (discrete time) model, such as damped oscillations and chaos. # Logistic growth {visibility="hidden"} ## From Geometric to Logistic Growth **Geometric growth** $$N_{t+1} = N_t + N_tr$$ . . . **Logistic growth** $$N_{t+1} = N_t + N_t r_{max}\left(1 - \frac{N_t}{K}\right)$$ . . . where ::: {style="font-size: 80%;"} - $r_{max}$ is the growth rate when $N_t$ is close to 0 - $K$ is the carrying capacity ::: ## Density-dependent growth
Logistic growth is an example of **density-dependent growth**. . . .
**Definition**: Population growth rate [is]{style="color: red;"} affected by population size ($N$). . . .
**Implications**: Resources are limited and there is a carrying capacity. ## Graphical depiction ::: {.cell} :::
::: {.r-stack} ::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/geom-1){width="90%"} ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=1} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/geom-logistic-1){width="90%"} ::: :::
## Growth rate ::: {style="font-size: 70%;"} $$\lambda_t = N_{t+1}/N_t$$ :::
![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/lr1-1){width="70%"} ::: {.fragment} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/lambda-1){width="70%"} :::
## Growth ::: {style="font-size: 70%;"} $$\Delta_t=N_{t+1}-N_t$$ :::
![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/lr2-1){width="70%"} ::: {.fragment} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/delta-1){width="70%"} :::
## Growth as a function of $N$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/delta-N-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ## What happens when we change $r_{max}$? ::: {.cell} :::
::: {.r-stack} ::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/Nl-1){width="80%"} ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-in-and-out fragment-index=1} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/Nl2-1){width="80%"} ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-in-and-out fragment-index=2} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/Nl3-1){width="80%"} ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-in-and-out fragment-index=3} ![](lecture-logistic-growth_files/figure-revealjs/Nl4-1){width="80%"} ::: :::
## Definitions
**Overcompensation** Density-dependent response in which populations over- or under-shoot carrying capacity rather than approach it gradually.
. . . #### Chaos Highly variable deterministic dynamics that are extremely sensitive to small changes in parameters. # Assumptions {visibility="hidden"} ## Assumptions of basic model - $K$ and $r_{max}$ are constant - No sex or age effects or other sources of individual heterogeneity - No time lags - No stochasticity ## Does logistic growth occur in nature? Fruit fly (*Drosophila melanogaster*) in the lab^[Data from Pearl (1927). Figure from Krebs (2014)]
![](figs/logistic-drosophila)
## Does logistic growth occur in nature? Ibex (*Capra ibex*) in Switzerland^[Data from Sæther et al. (2002). Figure from Krebs (2014)]
[![](figs/logistic-ibex)](https://youtu.be/hqqCafpgSVA?si=greGPq4_wLm_BQLI)
# Summary {visibility="hidden"} ## **Summary** ::: {.incremental style="font-size: 75%;"} - Logistic growth is a form of density-dependent growth - Growth rate ($\lambda_t=N_{t+1}/N_t$) declines as $N$ approaches $K$ - Growth ($\Delta_t=N_{t+1}-N_t$) peaks at $K/2$ (the inflection point) - The model doesn't include birth, mortality, and movement processes, but it can be derived from density-dependent birth and death rates. - But it does allow for complex dynamics that resemble patterns seen in nature. ::: . . .
**Assignment**
Read pages 32--36 in Conroy and Carroll.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
